solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: One propping up the bar with old pals got tipsy

indicators.note: someone tipsy staggers about, so the letters before it lurch out of order

blocks.note: O is the standard abbreviation for old
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A pub regular leaning on the bar with his old friends, who have all got drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: The bar is not in a pub: it is the crossbar of a goal, held up by the uprights.
explanation.definitionFit: Each upright of a goal supports the crossbar at its top, so it literally holds up the bar.

clue.text: Perhaps Hertz van, lacking traction ultimately, overturned after a blast of wind

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the word traction
a word lacking something has had that letter taken away from it
in a down entry, something overturned is turned upside down, so read from the other end

blocks.note: a gust is a sudden blast of wind
taken as written
the last letter of traction, removed from van

explanation.surface: A rental van from Hertz loses grip and flips over in a gust of wind.
explanation.walkthrough: Hertz looks like the car-hire firm, but the definition is the physicist Gustav Hertz; 'Perhaps' signals he is one example of a Gustav.
explanation.definitionFit: Gustav Hertz was a German Nobel-winning physicist, so he is an example of someone with this first name.

clue.text: An American incorporating a company emblem which is similar

indicators.note: incorporating means taking something into the body of another, so one piece sits inside the other

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
a logo is a company's emblem
US, the abbreviation for the United States, stands for American

explanation.surface: An American firm's logo that resembles another one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'An American' is read as two words that split apart so the emblem can sit between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Analogous describes things comparable or alike in some respect, a close synonym of similar.

clue.text: It's used to make a point by a writer keen to back Descartes

definitions.text: It's used to make a point

indicators.note: to back here means going backwards, so the name is read from its end

blocks.note: a pencil is something you write with
a keen blade is a sharp one
the philosopher's first name, read backwards here

explanation.surface: A philosopher making a point, with a writer eager to support Descartes.
explanation.walkthrough: René Descartes was the French philosopher of 'I think, therefore I am'; 'make a point' is literal, not argumentative.
explanation.definitionFit: This gadget shaves wood from a pencil tip to give it a fine sharp point again.

clue.text: Manage to retain ferocious outside left

indicators.note: one word placed outside another wraps around it on both sides

blocks.note: savage means fierce or ferocious
L is the standard abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: Coping with keeping a ferocious player on the outside left of the team.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outside left' reads like a football position, but 'outside' is the instruction to wrap SAVAGE round L.
explanation.definitionFit: To salvage something is to rescue it from loss, so you manage to keep hold of it.

clue.text: Counsel's weakness of character evident after today

indicators.note: showing up after something places this piece behind the other one

blocks.note: AD, anno domini, labels the present era of dates
a vice is a moral failing or weakness of character

explanation.surface: A barrister's flaw of character becomes obvious in the present day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Counsel's' is 'Counsel is'; it looks like a lawyer, but the definition is the noun meaning guidance.
explanation.definitionFit: Counsel in the sense of guidance offered to someone is a synonym of recommendation or advice.

clue.text: The trial fee incited riots

indicators.note: riots is a verb here: the letters run riot and end up in disorder

blocks.note: taken as written, all fifteen letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A legal charge for a trial sparks riots in the streets.
explanation.walkthrough: The opening word looks like a mere article to skip, but it is the whole definition.
explanation.definitionFit: In grammar, 'the' is the English word classed as the definite article, as opposed to 'a' or 'an'.

clue.text: Run into a dog near the centre of Altrincham

indicators.note: the centre of a ten-letter word is its middle pair of letters

blocks.note: the fifth and sixth letters of the town's name
a cur is a mongrel dog

explanation.surface: Bumping into a dog close to the middle of Altrincham.
explanation.walkthrough: Altrincham is a town in Greater Manchester; 'Run into' is not meeting someone but incurring something such as debt.
explanation.definitionFit: To run into costs or trouble is to bring them on yourself, which is to incur them.

clue.text: Made beloved stop collecting expensive delftware finally

indicators.note: finally picks out the last letter of the word before it
a word collecting others gathers them up inside itself

blocks.note: to end something is to stop it
dear means costly
the last letter of delftware

explanation.surface: Someone who has made themselves cherished, then gives up buying pricey Dutch pottery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stop collecting' looks like giving up a hobby, but stop is the outer word and collecting the wrapping instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: To endear someone is to make them loved or liked, so the past tense means caused to be cherished.

clue.text: A French dance said to be amazing

indicators.note: said means spoken, so we want a word that sounds like the dance

blocks.note: un is French for a
a reel is a lively Scottish dance

explanation.surface: A French dance that is spoken of as wonderful.
explanation.definitionFit: Unreal is informal praise for something so incredible it seems impossible, close to astonishing.

clue.text: Cooks finally run out of seafood and eggs

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of the word before it
being out of something means that letter has gone from the word

blocks.note: the last letter of Cooks
a prawn is a shellfish eaten as seafood
R is the cricket abbreviation for run, removed from the shellfish

explanation.surface: The cooks have finally run out of seafood and eggs in the kitchen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Run out' looks like one phrase meaning exhausted supplies, but it splits into the letter to drop and the deletion signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Spawn is the mass of eggs laid in water by fish, frogs or shellfish.

clue.text: Had a strong desire to hold fellow to account for having a miserable expression

indicators.note: a word that holds others keeps them inside it

blocks.note: longed means yearned for
F is the abbreviation for fellow
AC is the abbreviation for account

explanation.surface: Someone wanted to make a man answer for looking so glum.
explanation.definitionFit: Long-faced describes someone looking sad or gloomy, with a drooping, dismal face.

clue.text: Detest weird toe mania going round Belgium

indicators.note: something weird is strange and out of normal shape, so the letters get rearranged
going round something means surrounding it, so the abbreviation sits within

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
B is the international vehicle code for Belgium

explanation.surface: Loathing a strange foot obsession that is spreading around Belgium.
explanation.definitionFit: To abominate is to loathe intensely, a strong synonym of hate.

clue.text: Girl taking in Mozart's earliest opera

indicators.note: earliest points to the first letter of the composer's name
taking in means admitting something inside

blocks.note: Nora is a girl's name
the first letter of Mozart

explanation.surface: A girl learning Mozart's earliest opera.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mozart's earliest opera' reads as one phrase, but the opera is Bellini's, not Mozart's.
explanation.definitionFit: Norma is Bellini's 1831 opera about a druid priestess, famous for the aria Casta diva.

clue.text: Animal eating bit of straw from a dish

indicators.note: a bit of a word is a single letter of it, here its opening one
a creature eating something takes it inside itself

blocks.note: a mouse is a small animal
the first letter of straw

explanation.surface: A creature nibbling a piece of straw out of its bowl.
explanation.definitionFit: A mousse is a light whipped dish, sweet or savoury, served as a course.

clue.text: Short note about decomposed rat discovered in waste disposal unit

indicators.note: something decomposed has broken down, so the letters fall apart and re-form
about means around, so the note goes round the other letters

blocks.note: a line is a brief letter, as in drop me a line
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A brief message about a rotting rat found in the waste disposal unit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short note' tempts you to shorten a musical note, but the whole phrase is a brief letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A latrine is a basic toilet, often a trench in a camp, so it disposes of human waste.

clue.text: Embarrassed by harsh command given to troops

blocks.note: ill can mean unkind or harsh, as in ill treatment
at ease is the order letting soldiers relax their stance

explanation.surface: Someone is upset by a harsh order barked at soldiers.
explanation.walkthrough: The drill order lets soldiers stand with feet apart and hands behind them.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone ill at ease is uncomfortable or awkward, close in feeling to being embarrassed.

clue.text: They're enthusiastic in a game set up among friends

indicators.note: in a down entry, set up means raised, so the word reads bottom to top
something among others is placed in their midst

blocks.note: taken as written
mates are friends
RU stands for rugby union

explanation.surface: Keen people playing in a match arranged among friends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'They're enthusiastic' is fair because an amateur, from Latin amare, plays for love rather than pay.
explanation.definitionFit: Amateurs pursue an activity for love of it rather than money, so they are keen devotees.

clue.text: It's hot information, regarded as scandalous, involving a leading performer

indicators.note: involving means wrapping something up within, so one piece holds the other

blocks.note: mud is damaging gossip, as in mud-slinging
a star is a leading performer

explanation.surface: Hot gossip about a scandal surrounding a celebrity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It's hot' reads like the start of a tabloid tease, but it defines a hot condiment.
explanation.definitionFit: Mustard is a pungent condiment whose spicy bite is described as hot.

clue.text: Brought back head of languages to help over manuscript of poor quality

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter
one word laid over another covers it on both sides here
brought back means returned the other way, so everything reads from the end

blocks.note: the first letter of languages
aid means help
MS is the abbreviation for manuscript

explanation.surface: A head of languages was recalled to help with a poorly written manuscript.
explanation.walkthrough: The reversal applies to the whole string built from the three pieces, not just the first one.
explanation.definitionFit: Dismal can mean pitifully bad or inadequate, as in a dismal performance.

clue.text: Not likely to fail in attempt against the French

blocks.note: to have a stab is to make an attempt
le is French for the; against means it follows on

explanation.surface: A confident bid made against the French.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Against' here means beside, leaning on the first piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Something stable is steady and secure, so unlikely to collapse or give way.

clue.text: Game fish about to return

indicators.note: to return is to come back the other way, so the word is read backwards

blocks.note: a snook is a tropical sea fish
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: Game fish are about to come back upstream.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Game fish' reads as one phrase, a fish caught for sport, but Game is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Snooker is a cue game played on a large baize table with fifteen reds and six colours.

clue.text: Optimistic over getting Ecstasy in club

indicators.note: in means placed inside the next word

blocks.note: up means finished, as in time is up
a bat is a club used to hit a ball
E is slang for the drug Ecstasy

explanation.surface: Feeling cheerful after taking Ecstasy at a nightclub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Club' suggests a nightclub, which is why drugs fit the scene; it is the hitting kind.
explanation.definitionFit: Upbeat means cheerful and positive in outlook, a synonym of hopeful.

clue.text: Side from the East touring Malta in March

indicators.note: in an across entry, coming from the East means reading right to left
touring a place means going round it, so the letters surround it

blocks.note: a part is a side in a dispute, as in take someone's part
M is the international vehicle code for Malta

explanation.surface: A team from the East goes on a tour of Malta in the month of March.
explanation.walkthrough: March looks like the month, capitalised as the first word of its phrase, but it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To tramp is to walk with heavy steady steps over a long distance, much like marching.

clue.text: Girl having a large dessert

blocks.note: taken as written
L is the abbreviation for large, as on clothing sizes
an ice is a frozen dessert

explanation.surface: A girl eating a big pudding.
explanation.definitionFit: Alice is a common female first name, as in Lewis Carroll's heroine.

clue.text: Curt gets second best position in American sport

blocks.note: a curt reply is a short one
S is the abbreviation for second
top means the best

explanation.surface: Curt is awarded second-best place in an American game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Curt' looks like a man's name; 'second best' looks like one phrase but splits in two.
explanation.definitionFit: In baseball the shortstop is the fielder stationed between second and third base.

clue.text: A standard upheld by Poles

blocks.note: surface reading: a principle or benchmark maintained by people from Poland
setter's reading: a standard is a flag, raised up on flagpoles

explanation.walkthrough: Capitalising Poles makes them Polish people, but they are the posts a flag flies from; a standard is a flag.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the national flag of the United Kingdom, flown hoisted on flagpoles across Britain.

clue.text: Stop legal action to arrest Earl

indicators.note: arresting someone means seizing and holding them, so a letter is held inside

blocks.note: a case is a lawsuit
E is the abbreviation for Earl

explanation.surface: Halt the lawsuit seeking to have a nobleman arrested.
explanation.definitionFit: To cease is to come to an end or halt, a formal synonym of the verb.

clue.text: Try to block extremely serious cuts

indicators.note: extremely points to the extremes of the word, its first and last letters
to block something is to sit in its way, inside it

blocks.note: the first and last letters of serious
to hear a case is to try it in court

explanation.surface: An attempt to stop very serious spending cuts.
explanation.walkthrough: Try is the judge's verb, not an attempt.
explanation.definitionFit: Shears, as a verb, means cuts with blades, as when shearing a sheep's fleece.

clue.text: Existing for the least amount of time as a celebration of cheese

definitions.text: Existing for the least amount of time

blocks.note: Brie is a soft French cheese
a fest is a festival or celebration

explanation.surface: A cheese festival that lasts only a very short while.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces read in reverse clue order: the cheese, then the party.
explanation.definitionFit: Briefest is the superlative of brief, meaning lasting the shortest time.
